quarterly_data.signal: Oncology Phase III outcomes in the H1 2026 results (R&D events from 29 April to 26 July 2026) not detailed on the call: EMERALD-2 (Imfinzi plus bevacizumab as adjuvant therapy in HCC at high risk of recurrence) did not meet its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival versus placebo. In NILE (1st-line PD-L1 high unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer) Imfinzi plus chemotherapy met one dual primary endpoint with a statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS improvement versus chemotherapy, while Imfinzi plus Imjudo with chemotherapy did not meet the other dual primary endpoint of OS. EMERALD-3 data presented in June showed the STRIDE regimen with lenvatinib and TACE reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 30% versus TACE alone (PFS HR 0.70; 95% CI 0.57-0.86; p=0.0007; median PFS 13.0 versus 9.8 months), with a positive OS trend (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.65-1.09; p=0.1814). Recruitment into PACIFIC-8 (Imfinzi plus domvanalimab in PD-L1 positive Stage III unresectable NSCLC) was discontinued based on the Arcus/Gilead STAR-121 and STAR-221 results.
quarterly_data.figure: EMERALD-2 RFS primary endpoint not met; NILE one of two OS dual primary endpoints met; EMERALD-3 PFS HR 0.70, median PFS 13.0 vs 9.8 months, OS HR 0.84; PACIFIC-8 recruitment discontinued

quarterly_data.signal: Regulatory decisions and filings listed in the H1 2026 results beyond those on the call: Japan approved Calquence as a fixed-duration regimen with venetoclax in CLL (AMPLIFY, June 2026), Etcamah (SERENA-6, June 2026) and perioperative Imfinzi with FLOT chemotherapy in resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (MATTERHORN, June 2026); China approved Orpathys for MET-amplified gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after at least two prior systemic treatments (July 2026); Fasenra was approved for hypereosinophilic syndrome (NATRON) in the US, Japan and China in May 2026 and in the EU in July 2026. Imfinzi with BCG was approved in the US for BCG-naive high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (POTOMAC, May 2026), but the EU Type II variation for that indication was voluntarily withdrawn in July 2026. The CHMP gave a positive opinion for Enhertu plus pertuzumab in 1st-line HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (DESTINY-Breast09, July 2026). In China the Lynparza PROfound indication (BRCAm mCRPC) was removed from the label after its conditional approval lapsed because the post-marketing commitment was not fulfilled (June 2026). New submissions or acceptances: Baxfendy in Japan (BaxHTN / Bax24 / BaxAsia), tozorakimab for COPD in the EU and China (OBERON / TITANIA / MIRANDA / PROSPERO) and efzimfotase alfa for HPP in Japan.
quarterly_data.figure: approvals: Calquence, Etcamah, Imfinzi (JP); Orpathys (CN); Fasenra HES (US, JP, CN, EU); Imfinzi POTOMAC (US); EU POTOMAC application withdrawn; Lynparza PROfound indication removed in China; filings: Baxfendy (JP), tozorakimab (EU, CN), efzimfotase alfa (JP)

quarterly_data.signal: elecoglipron Phase IIb numbers presented at ADA in June 2026: in VISTA (adults with obesity or overweight and at least one comorbidity) elecoglipron produced an average body-weight reduction of 10.5% at 26 weeks versus 0.6% with placebo (a dual primary endpoint), with no plateau, reaching 11.8% at 36 weeks (75mg) versus 0.3% with placebo; in SOLSTICE (type 2 diabetes) it reduced HbA1c by 1.9% from baseline at 26 weeks versus 0.2% with placebo, the trial's primary endpoint.
quarterly_data.figure: VISTA weight loss 10.5% vs 0.6% at 26 weeks, 11.8% vs 0.3% at 36 weeks (75mg); SOLSTICE HbA1c reduction 1.9% vs 0.2% at 26 weeks

quarterly_data.signal: Rare Disease trial numbers in the H1 2026 results: the Ultomiris I CAN Phase III prespecified interim analysis in IgAN showed a 46.6% reduction in 24-hour UPCR from baseline at week 34 versus 5.6% with placebo, a placebo-adjusted treatment effect of 43.4% (95% CI 33.5%-51.8%; p<0.0001). The ALXN1210-MG-319 Phase III single-arm, open-label trial of Ultomiris in paediatric and adolescent generalised myasthenia gravis met its primary endpoints with efficacy consistent with adults (new disclosure, July 2026). The anselamimab CARES results (62% survival improvement, HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.17-0.86, nominal p=0.012; 71% fewer cardiovascular hospitalisations, incidence risk ratio 0.29, nominal p=0.028) come from a prespecified subgroup of patients with kappa predominant light chain isotype. In CALYPSO, 31.1% of eneboparatide patients met the composite primary endpoint (serum calcium within normal range and independence from oral supplements at week 24) versus 5.9% on placebo (n=41/132 vs n=4/68; p=0.0001). For efzimfotase alfa, MULBERRY showed a median RGI-C score of 1.67 at week 25 versus 0 on placebo (p=0.0003) in children 2 to <12 years, and in CHESTNUT treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 90.5% of children who switched from Strensiq versus 86.4% who stayed on Strensiq.
quarterly_data.figure: I CAN UPCR reduction 46.6% vs 5.6%, placebo-adjusted 43.4%; MG-319 primary endpoints met; CARES kappa subgroup HR 0.38, IRR 0.29; CALYPSO 31.1% vs 5.9%; MULBERRY RGI-C 1.67 vs 0; CHESTNUT TEAE 90.5% vs 86.4%

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 results as filed (figures not given on the call): Total Revenue was $30,672m (H1 2025: $28,045m), up 9% actual and 6% at CER, and Q2 Total Revenue was $15,384m (up 6% actual, 5% at CER); Core EPS was $5.21 for H1 and $2.63 for Q2 (up 18% at CER), with a Core Operating Margin of 34% in both H1 and Q2. By region in H1: US $12,890m (+8%), Europe $6,822m (+8% at CER), Emerging Markets ex. China $4,809m (+10% at CER) and China $3,510m (-5% at CER; -13% at CER in Q2). Medicine detail: Imfinzi H1 $3,548m (+29% at CER), Ultomiris Q2 $1,314m, Strensiq Q2 $536m, Lynparza Q2 $829m (-3% at CER), Koselugo H1 $347m (+21% at CER), Wainua Q2 $70m (+58%), Beyfortus Q2 $79m (-37%), and first sales of $3m each for Baxfendy and Etcamah. Partner-combined sales in H1: Enhertu $2,961m (H1 2025: $2,289m), Datroway $225m (H1 2025: $45m) and Tezspire $1,150m (H1 2025: $826m). Q2 impairment charges against products in development were $345m. The Core Tax rate is expected to be between 18-22% for FY 2026.

quarterly_data.signal: Patent and dispute developments disclosed with the H1 2026 results: in July 2026 the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit affirmed that the Wyeth patents asserted against Tagrisso are invalid (a 2024 jury had awarded Wyeth $107.5m). Forxiga patents face validity challenges in Europe: the Polish Patent Office invalidated one in February 2026 (AstraZeneca is appealing), a Portuguese validity trial concluded in July 2026 with judgment reserved, and a French trial is scheduled for June 2027; in Australia AstraZeneca obtained a preliminary injunction in March 2026 against Pharmacor's dapagliflozin launch. In the UK it brought a Tagrisso patent infringement action against Hansoh over the prospective commercialisation of aumolertinib (trial June 2027) and challenged the MHRA and EMA marketing authorisations for aumolertinib. It settled the University of Sheffield dispute over the Lynparza patent licence for a payment of $220m in May 2026. In June 2026 it commenced an ICC arbitration against Sanofi Pasteur over alleged non-performance under the Beyfortus collaboration agreement, and Sanofi has filed counterclaims (Beyfortus revenue includes AstraZeneca's Product Sales of manufactured product to Sanofi).
quarterly_data.figure: Tagrisso: Wyeth patents held invalid on appeal ($107.5m jury award); Sheffield settlement $220m; Forxiga patent challenges in Poland, Portugal, France
